title: General-alphabet Hamming oracles with optimal preprocessing
formal: Is there a uniform deterministic data structure which, for every pair of strings of lengths \(n,m\ge1\) and every integer \(1\le x\le\min(n,m)\), uses \(\widetilde O(nm/x)\) preprocessing time and stored words and answers exact substring Hamming-distance queries in \(O(x)\) worst-case time?
definitions: The strings \(A\) and \(B\) are supplied explicitly over \([0..(n+m)^2)\). A query \((i,j,\ell)\) satisfies \(0\le i\le n\), \(0\le j\le m\), and \(0\le\ell\le\min(n-i,m-j)\). It returns \(|\{t:0\le t<\ell,\ A[i+t]\ne B[j+t]\}|\). Positions are zero-based; a length-zero query returns zero. Set \(L=n+m\). Use a uniform sequential word RAM with word length \(w=d\lceil\log_2(L+2)\rceil\), for a fixed integer \(d\ge 8\) chosen with the algorithm. A fixed finite program must handle every input size; there is no advice, precomputed lookup table or input-dependent oracle. Unit-cost operations are reads, writes, copying, comparisons, branching, Boolean operations, logical shifts, addition, subtraction and multiplication modulo \(2^w\), and integer quotient and remainder for a nonzero divisor. Shifts by at least \(w\) return zero. Addresses and stored values fit words; multiword operations pay for their constituent instructions. All initialization, preprocessing, tables and output writes are charged. A static query starts without input-dependent private state, and every retained copy of the input or auxiliary information counts toward index space. The soft-O means multiplication by \((\log(L+2))^c\) for one fixed constant \(c\), independent of \(x,n,m\). One fixed algorithm receives \(x\) during preprocessing and handles all admissible parameters. The stored space includes both strings, if retained, and all auxiliary information. Query space is included; no offline knowledge of future queries is supplied. More explicitly, there must be constants \(C\ge1\), \(c\ge0\) and \(d\ge8\), independent of all input parameters, such that preprocessing uses at most \(C(nm/x)(\log_2(L+2))^c\) operations, total stored and query workspace uses at most that many words, and every query takes at most \(Cx\) operations. The constants can absorb the finitely many smallest inputs. No randomness or error is allowed.

context_blocks.text: Hamming distance counts mismatched positions in two equal-length strings. Here the input is a fixed pair of longer strings, but each query chooses its own pair of starting positions and common length. The output is a single exact integer, so the query need not list the mismatches.

For example, with \(A=(1,2,1,3)\) and \(B=(1,3,1,2)\), the query \((0,0,4)\) returns two, while \((1,1,2)\) returns one. The starting positions may differ, and neither interval must be a prefix. Symbols are arbitrary integers in the specified range; their numerical differences have no role.

The parameter \(x\) specifies a family of preprocessing–query compromises for the same task. When \(n=m\), the target includes nearly quadratic preprocessing with constant query time at \(x=1\), and nearly linear preprocessing with linear query time at \(x=n\). Every intermediate value must be handled by the same uniform algorithm.

Boneh and coauthors obtain \(\widetilde O(nm/x)\) preprocessing and \(O(x)\) exact query time for constant alphabets. Their general polynomial-integer-alphabet bound is \(\widetilde O(nm/\sqrt{x})\) preprocessing with the same query time. The card retains the previously selected deterministic question of removing this preprocessing gap.

The paper also gives approximate randomized oracles. Their guarantees allow an error in the reported distance and therefore concern a different output requirement. The present proposition requires exact answers on every query and has no probabilistic success qualification.

The source lower bound assumes a hypothesis about combinatorial matrix multiplication and applies to combinatorial oracles. The target here allows all operations in the stated word RAM. That restricted conditional result therefore does not establish an unconditional optimum or refute the proposed general-alphabet bound.

why: This isolates the cost of reusable exact similarity queries and tests whether large alphabets create an inherent preprocessing penalty.
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean of the stated proposition or its logical negation, with the same model, quantifiers and resource guarantees. A conditional lower bound establishes only its conditional conclusion. An improvement that does not meet the full target is insufficient.

progress.text: The CPM 2026 paper proves the exact constant-alphabet tradeoff and the larger \(\widetilde O(nm/\sqrt{x})\) general-alphabet preprocessing bound. Its separate approximation results and conditional combinatorial lower bound do not settle this deterministic exact endpoint.

status_note: The CPM 2026 source establishes a weaker general-alphabet preprocessing bound. A bounded source and later-work check on 14 September 2026 found no resolution of the selected deterministic endpoint. The reported conditional combinatorial lower bound does not cover all allowed algorithms; source proofs were not independently formalized.

sentences: Two strings are preprocessed before their substring comparisons are known.
Each query requests the exact Hamming distance between equal-length intervals.
A parameter controls the allowed query time.
The proposed preprocessing bound matches the constant-alphabet regime.
Current general-alphabet bounds have a square-root loss in that parameter.
